title: Will Ye No Come Back Again?
description: Lady Nairne's song for Bonnie Prince Charlie, for 2 to 4 singers: two verses, each with the chorus "Will ye no come back again?". The soprano sings the melody, the alto sings the words beneath it, the tenor fills in the chord, and the bass sings the roots. Tender and moderate; the tune runs from low C to high F, a little wider than a beginner's comfortable range.

credits.tune: as printed under Finlay Dun's name (1795 to 1853)

licence.words: public domain: Carolina Oliphant, Lady Nairne, died 1845; words as printed with this tune in Gems of Scottish Song (Oliver Ditson & Co., Boston), 1894 printing, p. 119 (verse 1 and the chorus read the same in the 1883 printing); verse 2 ends "Death or exile braving" as both printings have it, where Charles Rogers's 1869 edition of her songs has "Your cleadin was but barely"
licence.tune: public domain: the tune as printed in Gems of Scottish Song (Oliver Ditson & Co., Boston; the printing catalogued as 1883), p. 107, headed "Finlay Dun." (Dun died 1853; the page does not say whether he wrote the air or arranged it)
licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella (its chords simpler than, and checked against, Finlay Dun's printed piano accompaniment)
licence.source: melody and verse 1 and chorus words from "Will Ye No Come Back Again?", headed "Finlay Dun.", in Gems of Scottish Song: A Collection of the Most Beautiful Scotch Ballads (Boston: Oliver Ditson & Co., the printing catalogued as 1883; publisher's editor unnamed), p. 107, printed in F in 4/4, "In moderate time", the tune on its own staff over a piano accompaniment; written here in F; read from the scan at archive.org/details/gemsofscottishso0000vari (leaf n105); every pitch and rhythm as printed; checked against the 1894 printing of the same book, p. 119, headed "Lady Nairne. (1766-1845)" and "Finlay Dun" (archive.org/details/gemsscottishson00unkngoog, leaf n133), whose re-engraving matches except one stray C in bar 6, so the notes follow 1883; verse 2's words from the 1894 printing ("Hieland" and "kent", Lady Nairne's Scots, where the 1883 printing has "High-land" and "kept"); verses 1 and 2 of the five printed, each followed by the chorus; verse 1 starts on the downbeat as printed, and verse 2's "Ye" is the printed pickup note and its "They" the printed small cue note C before bar 3; the grace note A before the second "gain?" and the fermatas left out; "be" for the printed "be" with a dash; breaths written in for beginners: the last note of every line ("wa", "main", "twa", "gain", "men", "lie", "glen", "ing", and each chorus "gain" and "be") shortened by three quarters of a beat, and the chorus's last "gain" before verse 2 cut to three quarters of a beat to leave room for "Ye"; in verse 2 the harmony parts sing "Char-" on the tune's A and "lie!" with its G, and "ing" with the F of the tune's "brav-", a beat or half a beat before the tune's syllable; Dun's dates (born 1795, died 1853) as Alfred Moffat prints them in The Minstrelsy of Scotland (London: Augener), in the note to "By yon bonnie banks", archive.org/details/minstrelsyofscot00moff
